question: A 30-year-old woman presents to her primary care provider complaining of intermittent fever and loss of appetite for the past 2 weeks. She is also concerned about painful genital lesions. Past medical history is noncontributory. She takes oral contraceptives and a multivitamin daily. She has had two male sexual partners in her lifetime and uses condoms inconsistently. She admits to being sexually active with 2 partners in the last 3 months and only using condoms on occasion. Today, her vitals are normal. On pelvic exam, there are red-rimmed, fluid-filled blisters over the labia minora (as seen in the photograph below) with swollen and tender inguinal lymph nodes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis of this patient?

paths: (Manual pelvic examination)-CAUSES->([X]Streptococcal septicemia, unspecified)-COMPLICATES->(Chronic tophaceous gout)-CAUSES->(Infection)-CAUSES->(genital herpes)

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Painful genital lesions with red-rimmed, fluid-filled blisters over the labia minora and swollen inguinal lymph nodes -> Genital herpes -> 95% CHAIN: Intermittent fever and loss of appetite -> Systemic symptoms -> Infectious etiology likely -> 80% CHAIN: Sexual history with multiple partners and inconsistent condom use -> Increased risk of sexually transmitted infections (STIs) -> 85% CHAIN: Pelvic exam findings of fluid-filled blisters over the labia minora -> Vesicular lesions characteristic of genital herpes -> 90% CHAIN: Swollen and tender inguinal lymph nodes -> Lymphadenopathy secondary to genital herpes infection -> 95%
enhanced_information: The most likely diagnosis for this patient with painful genital lesions, red-rimmed, fluid-filled blisters over the labia minora, and swollen inguinal lymph nodes is genital herpes. The patient's symptoms, sexual history, and pelvic exam findings are highly suggestive of genital herpes infection.
analysis: The patient's presentation of painful genital lesions with red-rimmed, fluid-filled blisters over the labia minora and swollen inguinal lymph nodes is highly suggestive of genital herpes. Given her sexual history and clinical findings, genital herpes is the most likely diagnosis.
